`case_study:sme-ipo-manipulation-2024-25` | 2025-11-28 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

India's SME platforms (BSE SME, NSE Emerge) saw a boom in 2023-24 with tiny issues oversubscribed hundreds of times. Cases: Varanium Cloud (NSE Emerge; raised Rs 40 cr in 2022 for data centres/learning centres, stock rallied many-fold) -- SEBI interim order May 2024 barred it and its promoter for inflated revenues and misuse of IPO money; Add-Shop E-Retail -- SEBI found manipulated financials to fuel the share price (2024); Resourceful Automobile (Aug 2024): a Rs 12 cr IPO for a two-showroom dealer oversubscribed ~400x drew public criticism; DroneAcharya (BSE SME) -- SEBI order (28 Nov 2025) fined the company/promoters Rs 75 lakh and barred them for up to two years for booking Rs 12.35 cr of income from entities that received no goods/services and inflating FY24 profits (company appealing); FOCL-linked SME IPOs -- SEBI found up to ~Rs 100 cr of IPO fund diversion (2025). SEBI tightened rules in 2025 (profitability track record, OFS limits, curbs on general corporate purposes; NSE capped listing-day gains). Visible flags: sudden revenue/profit jump in the 1-2 years pre-IPO; related-party customers/vendors; tiny float and extreme subscription; same merchant bankers across many problem issues; bonus/split + preferential allotments after listing; promoters exiting after lock-in; Telegram/WhatsApp tips. Lesson: treat SME IPOs as guilty until proven innocent; require multi-year audited CFO, check banker's past listings, and avoid on circuit-filter-driven price runs.

**Lesson:** SME IPOs: assume promoter-driven pricing; verify CFO
**Spotted early by:** SEBI forensic audits; Value Research, journalists
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:disqualifiers`, illustrates -> `insight:forensic-redflag-checklist`, similar_to -> `case_study:gensol-2025`
**Sources:** <https://inc42.com/buzz/sebi-cracks-down-on-droneacharya-founders-over-ipo-fraud-revenue-inflation> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/markets/ipo/accounting-fraud-concerns-raise-red-flags-for-india-s-booming-tiny-ipos-124051400388_1.html> ; <https://moneylife.in/article/sebi-finds-up-to-rs100-crore-fund-diversion-in-focllinked-sme-ipos-report/78805.html> ; <https://www.valueresearchonline.com/stories/222267/spotting-sme-ipo-traps-varanium-cloud-scam/> ; <https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/circulars/INVG71553.pdf>

body:
`case_study:monster-beverage-2002-2024` · tickers US-MNST · confidence: verified

Hansen's (1935 juice co.) went bankrupt 1988; Rodney Sacks and Hilton Schlosberg bought it and listed it 1990 at pennies. 1990s energy drinks went nowhere; the Monster brand launched 2002 and the company took off. CNBC: ~+200,000% from Feb 1994 to Feb 2024 ($1k -> ~$2m; $55.02 close Feb 2024); ~42% CAGR over the 20 years to 2023 (BusinessTech). Splits 2:1 2005, 4:1 2006, 2:1 2012, 3:1 2016, 2:1 2023 (96x cumulative): a ~$5 2003 Hansen share is ~$0.05 today [split math mine; 2003 price unverified]. Max drawdown: roughly -70% in 2007-08 [unverified]. Growth was overwhelmingly sales/EPS (31 consecutive years of sales growth); P/E rose from low-teens to 30-40x [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2003-05: a tiny company with a new brand growing sales >50%/yr, ~50% gross margins, fully outsourced production (co-packers) and distribution through beer distributors (capital-light), plus action-sports marketing creating a youth category. Coca-Cola's 16.7% stake for >$2bn (2014) and 2015 distribution swap were late confirmation, not the signal. Who caught it: the insiders (Sacks/Schlosberg, large owners); no well-documented famous early outside investor found. Stall: growth slowed to low-teens by 2023-24; stock range-bound ~2021-24. LESSON: a boring-looking small consumer company that creates a category, outsources the capital, and keeps the same owner-managers can compound for decades; the obvious-in-hindsight signal was unit growth + gross margin + zero capex, not a famous holder.

- **Start → end:** ~$0.05 split-adj (2003) [unverified] → $55.02 (Feb 2024) (~+200,000% from 1994 (CNBC); ~1,000x from 2003 [est])
- **EPS vs rerating:** mostly EPS/sales growth; P/E low-teens -> 30-40x [unverified]
- **Max drawdown:** ~-70% 2007-08 [unverified]
- **Early signal:** new brand >50% sales growth, ~50% GM, outsourced bottling + beer-distributor network
- **Who caught it:** founder-owners Sacks/Schlosberg; Coca-Cola 2014 (late)
- **Ended/stalled:** growth slowed 2022-24, stock range-bound
- **Lesson:** category creation + capital-light + owner-managers
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.cnbc.com/2024/02/17/monster-energy-drink-stock-is-best-performer-of-the-last-30-years.html) · [2](https://businesstech.co.za/news/finance/682867/monster-growth-over-two-decades-turning-r1000-into-r3-1-million/) · [3](https://www.morningstar.com.au/personal-finance/seven-lessons-from-one-of-the-best-stocks-in-history)

body: **Summary:** Retailers make money on gross margin times sales density (sales per sq ft) minus rent and staff. Returns depend on store-level economics: payback period, sales per sq ft and same-store sales growth, scaled through cluster expansion. QSR franchisees (Jubilant, Devyani, Sapphire, Westlife) pay royalties to the brand owner (Domino's, Yum, McDonald's) and earn on unit economics: ADS, SSSG, gross margin on food and delivery mix. Key metrics: SSSG/LFL, revenue per sq ft or ADS, store additions and store-level EBITDA, gross margin, inventory turns (retail), payback period, pre-Ind AS EBITDA (rent-adjusted), and RoCE. Cycle drivers: urban discretionary spend, food inflation, competition (quick commerce, aggregators, value formats), rental costs, and consumer down-trading. Lead indicators: Retailers Association of India monthly growth, mall footfall trackers, credit card spends (RBI monthly), Swiggy/Zomato GOV, company quarterly business updates, urban consumer confidence (RBI CCS). Winners (DMart on everyday low cost with owned stores, Trent on private-label fashion, Westside/Zudio, Jubilant through its 2010–15 expansion) kept store economics superior, a private-label or cost model and disciplined rollout. Losers (Future Group on debt and over-expansion, Shoppers Stop, Café Coffee Day on governance) expanded faster than the economics allowed. Valuation: EV/EBITDA 30–60x and P/E 70–120x for DMart and Trent at peaks. QSR is valued at EV/sales or pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA. Nov 2026: QSR LFL is recovering slowly (Domino's India LFL 4.1% in Q2 FY27 against 2.5% in Q1; Devyani SSSG 4–9% ex-Pizza Hut, revenue +10.4%). Traps: store-count growth with falling SSSG, and Ind AS 116 flattering EBITDA. Sources: [1](https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/jubilant-foodworks-q2-fy27-revenue-rises-11-9-percent/) · [2](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/devyani-q2-fy27-revenue-growth-cmw3eq4cz009s2mph8cf1rlji) Links: about `person:radhakishan-damani`

body:
`insight:india-mb-drawdowns-base-rate` · confidence: verified

Maximum peak-to-trough fall inside each winner's own up-move (weekly closes), 27 windows: median −41%; 22 of 27 (81%) had at least one ≥30% drawdown, and 14 (52%) at least one ≥40%. Examples: Bajaj Finance −61% (2020), Tata Elxsi −59% (2018–20), APL Apollo −57% (2018–19), BSE −55% (2022–23), Dixon −52% (2021–23), Page −52% (2018–20), Avanti −51% (2012–13), Balkrishna −48%, HAL −47% (2020), Caplin −47% (2013), Polycab −45%, CDSL −44%. The shallowest were Pidilite (−26%), Eicher 2008–17 (−26%), Trent 2020–24 (−22%) and Kaynes (−20%, a short run). Most of these drawdowns came from market shocks (2013 taper, 2018 small-cap crash, 2020 COVID) or de-rating while EPS kept rising (Caplin 2017–20: EPS 2x, price −68%), not from broken theses. Holding rule: a ≥40% fall is the normal cost of a multibagger. The question at −40% is whether EPS and ROCE are intact (hold or add) or the driver has broken (exit). Position size so a −60% move is survivable. Extends insight:winners-drawdowns to India.

Links: `insight:winners-drawdowns` (part_of), `strategy:position-sizing` (about), `case_study:caplin-point-2009-2026` (about), `case_study:bajaj-finance-2009-2021` (about)

Pre-registered split test (`research_notes/Backtests/survival_cap_split_india.md`; note: prereg was written first but committed together
with results, so the git timestamp doesn't prove order — the stage log does). Pledge-only does NOT cut the upside in the event sample
(3x-winner RR 1.27 [0.77, 1.88]); single-flag tails swap by regime (pledge bad 2018–21, weak ICR bad 2022–25). Only **both flags**
is consistently bad: 12m halving 4.2×, 3y failure 9.4×, stable across periods and the survivorship-free panel — yet still 23.5% triple.
Card unchanged. Judgement rule until tested: when both flags fire, answer the balance-sheet question before even a starter position.
Next: pre-register "both flags → 0 new money" on fresh 2026+ events.
